Turn 1 correctly carries `request.cache_salt`, but the tool-continuation re-submission rebuilds the engine input via `tokens_input(token_ids)` with **no** `cache_salt`. The continuation prefix is therefore cached in the global *unsalted* namespace even though the caller opted into salting. A second tenant who can guess the low-entropy post-tool history submits the reconstructed continuation (unsalted) and reads exact per-turn cached-token counts from the Responses usage — restoring the prompt-membership oracle that `cache_salt` is documented to prevent.  Silently dropping a preserved salt *after* the supported tool workflow is enabled is a broken isolation control: the caller enabled salting and every turn should stay isolated, but continuation turns leak into the shared cache.  This is distinct from [GHSA-4qjh-9fv9-r85r](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/security/advisories/GHSA-4qjh-9fv9-r85r) ([CVE-2025-46570](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-46570)): that advisory is the prefix-cache membership oracle for which `cache_salt` is the documented mitigation, and its PR-17045 fix does not close this site — the Harmony tool continuation silently drops the preserved salt, caching in the unsalted namespace and leaking exact `cached_tokens_per_turn` counts from a different sink (the Responses serving continuation, not general TTFT timing).  ## Affected code  Links pinned to the confirmed commit [`752a3a504485`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34) (v0.25.1):  - **The documented control being defeated:** [`vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py#L235`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/752a3a504485790a2e8491cacbb35c137339ad34/vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/protocol.py#L235) (`cache_salt` field).  The tool-continuation re-submission rebuilds the engine input with no `cache_salt`:  ```python # vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py Lines 711-715             if isinstance(context, HarmonyContext):                 token_ids = context.render_for_completion()                 engine_input = tokens_input(token_ids)                  sampling_params.max_tokens = max_model_len - len(token_ids) ```  Contrast with the correct turn-1 call, which does preserve the caller's salt:  ```python # vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py Lines 754-755         prompt_token_ids = render_for_completion(messages)         engine_input = tokens_input(prompt_token_ids, cache_salt=request.cache_salt) ```  `tokens_input` stores the salt on the engine input only when it is passed, so the continuation input carries none and lands in the unsalted namespace:  ```python # vllm/inputs/engine.py Lines 51-66 def tokens_input(     prompt_token_ids: list[int],     *,     prompt: str | None = None,     cache_salt: str | None = None, ) -> TokensInput:     """     Construct [`TokensInput`][vllm.inputs.engine.TokensInput]     from optional values.     """     inputs = TokensInput(type="token", prompt_token_ids=prompt_token_ids)      if prompt is not None:         inputs["prompt"] = prompt     if cache_salt is not None:         inputs["cache_salt"] = cache_salt ```  ## Impact  An authenticated tenant of a shared deployment can recover whether a guessed post-tool prompt or history was processed by another tenant, with exact cached-token counts rather than noisy latency — the exact prompt-membership oracle `cache_salt` is documented to prevent. It defeats the multi-user prefix-cache isolation guarantee for salted Harmony tool sessions.  Preconditions: a GPT-OSS Harmony model on `/v1/responses`; prefix caching enabled (default); an operator-enabled built-in or MCP tool server; the victim sets `cache_salt` and triggers at least one tool continuation; and the attacker can reconstruct the post-tool history closely enough to match the token prefix. The `AC:H` metric reflects that guessable-history precondition.   ## Suggested Fix  Propagate `request.cache_salt` into every Harmony (and Parsable) tool-continuation re-submission — at the continuation call site call `tokens_input(token_ids, cache_salt=request.cache_salt)`, mirroring the correct turn-1 call. Carry the salt on the `HarmonyContext` (thread the originating `request` into the context) so no continuation path can omit it:  ```diff # vllm/entrypoints/openai/responses/serving.py              if isinstance(context, HarmonyContext):                  token_ids = context.render_for_completion() -                engine_input = tokens_input(token_ids) +                engine_input = tokens_input( +                    token_ids, +                    cache_salt=( +                        context.request.cache_salt +                        if context.request is not None +                        else None +                    ), +                ) ```  with `HarmonyContext.__init__` gaining a `request: ResponsesRequest | None = None` parameter (stored as `self.request`) that `_create_responses` passes when constructing the context. The continuation prefix is then cached in the victim's salted namespace, mirroring turn 1.  Suggested regression test: assert `cached_tokens_per_turn == 0` for a different-salt probe against a salted victim continuation (the four-way control from the proof of concept).  ## Credit  **Reported by:** Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration)  This vulnerability was discovered using GPT-5.5-Cyber as part of the Patch the Planet security initiative.  ---  **Proposed fix:** a fix for this issue is proposed in a public pull request: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/51818

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.30.0, the Rust frontend's track_http_metrics middleware records the raw HTTP method token as a Prometheus label for requests reaching registered routes. An unauthenticated attacker can send unique arbitrary method tokens to unguarded routes such as /tokenize, causing Prometheus's Family::get_or_create function to permanently create counter and histogram label sets. Those label sets increase process memory usage and enlarge the /metrics response until the service or monitoring path is exhausted. This issue is fixed in version 0.30.0.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, an authenticated caller can place forged shared-memory address and monotonic_id values in public multimodal features.kwargs_data. In scale-out deployments with shared-memory multimodal caching enabled, workers trust those values and pass attacker-selected bytes to pickle.loads(), allowing arbitrary Python execution even when insecure serialization is disabled. This issue is fixed in version 0.32.0.

vLLM from 0.10.2 before 0.25.0 contains an uncontrolled resource consumption vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory because the Nemotron-VL processors globally set Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS to None. Attackers can submit a pathological decompression-bomb image to /v1/chat/completions to OOM-kill the worker and deny service to co-tenants.

vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. ChatParams.get_apply_chat_template_kwargs() preserves that value without enforcing trust_request_chat_template, so the request can bypass the intended trust policy and cause CPU or memory exhaustion through Jinja rendering. vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, the OpenAI-compatible server configures Starlette CORSMiddleware with allowed_origins set to a wildcard by default. A malicious web page can use a victim's browser to reach an unauthenticated vLLM server on localhost, an internal network, or a VPN, call endpoints including GET /v1/models and POST /v1/chat/completions, consume GPU resources, and read responses. Cookie-based cross-site request forgery does not apply because credentials are disabled by default, and deployments requiring bearer authentication are exposed only when the caller already has a usable token. vLLM is an inference and serving engine for large language models. Prior to 0.32.0, vllm/tokenizers/hf.py computes max_token_id with an off-by-one upper bound, allowing a pre-tokenized prompt ID equal to the vocabulary size to pass validation. For a tensor-parallel size of one and an exact multiple-of-64 vocabulary, VocabParallelEmbedding.forward does not mask that value before F.embedding uses it, causing a CUDA device-side assertion and terminating the engine. vLLM from 0.9.2 before 0.24.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows API callers to force outbound connections by embedding a decode address in the X-Request-Id header. ## Summary  Multimodal content parts (`image_url`, `video_url`, `input_audio`, ...) accept a user-supplied `uuid` field that vLLM uses **verbatim as the item's cache identity** (`mm_hash`). The two frontend/engine processor caches (P0 "sender" cache in the API process, P1 "receiver" cache in the EngineCore process) are independent LRU caches whose evictions are **not synchronized**, and the P1 hit path performs **zero consistency validation** — it silently substitutes the cached item's tensor data for whatever the current request actually contains.  A single unauthenticated client can exploit this to kill the entire engine, deterministically, with default server flags:  1. **Seed**: send a small image with `uuid="U"`. Both caches now map `U` to an item with **N_A** visual tokens (e.g. 4). 2. **Drift**: send ~70 requests, each carrying a *unique* uuid, a max-size image, and an over-long text prompt. Each request is rejected with 400 — but **after** its image has been inserted into the P0 cache (insertion happens during chat rendering, before prompt-length validation), so these requests fill P0 **without ever reaching the engine/P1**. `U` is evicted from P0 only. 3. **Kill**: send a *large* image with `uuid="U"`. P0 misses → the image is freshly processed and the prompt is spliced with **N_B** (e.g. 2048+) placeholder tokens; the request carries full data to the engine, but P1 still has `U` → the engine **discards the fresh data and substitutes the stale N_A-row tensor**. The scheduler plans for N_B encoder slots while the worker merges N_A embeddings into N_B placeholders → `ValueError: Attempted to assign 4 = 4 multimodal tokens to 2048 placeholders` at `vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:711` → uncaught in the EngineCore busy loop → `_send_engine_dead()` → the EngineCore process dies, every API server reports `EngineDeadError` and shuts down. `/health` never recovers; the deployment needs a full restart.  Verified end-to-end on the official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.29.0` image with Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, default configuration (no flags beyond `--served-model-name`/`--gpu-memory-utilization`): after 70 flood requests the kill request returned `500 EngineCore encountered an issue` and `/health` went dead permanently. The vulnerable code is byte-identical on `main` (post-0.29.0).  ## Details  **1. The client-controlled `uuid` becomes the cache hash verbatim.** `vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py:1677` / `:1884-1886` read `part["uuid"]` per content part and pass it through as `mm_uuids`. In `vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py:62-63`, when no `hf_processor_mm_kwargs` are present (the default for chat requests), the uuid string **is** the item hash — no content binding at all:  ```python # vllm/multimodal/processing/inputs.py:62-63 else:     hashes.append(uuid_item)        # client string used verbatim as mm_hash ```  **2. P0 insertion happens before request validation.** In the serving path, `render_chat_request` (`vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/serving.py:275`) runs full mm processing — `mm_processor.apply` (`vllm/renderers/base.py:759`) → `_cached_apply_hf_processor` → `_merge_mm_kwargs` → `cache.get_and_update_item` (`vllm/multimodal/processing/processor.py:1338`), which inserts the processed item into the P0 sender cache (default `mm_processor_cache_type="lru"`, 4 GiB). Only afterwards does `get_max_tokens` (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/utils/api_utils.py:183-186`) reject over-long prompts with 400. **A request can therefore write to P0 while never reaching the engine** — the primitive that desynchronizes P0 from P1. (Public issue #43941 documented this same asymmetry for the opposite drift direction, which was later handled via `MultiModalCacheMissError`; the P0-miss/P1-hit direction below was never addressed.)  **3. P1 substitutes cached data on hash hit with no consistency check.** In the EngineCore input thread, `preprocess_add_request` (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py:997-1000`) calls `mm_receiver_cache.get_and_update_features`, which only replaces `feature.data` (`vllm/multimodal/cache.py:673-690`) and keeps the request's own `mm_position` (placeholder layout). On a cache hit the receiver cache returns the stale item wholesale:  ```python # vllm/multimodal/cache.py:739-740  (MultiModalReceiverCache.get_and_update_item) if (cached_item := self._cache.get(mm_hash)) is not None:     return cached_item              # fresh data silently discarded; no size/modality check ```  Only the opposite drift (P0 hit / P1 miss, `data=None`) is handled, via the retryable `MultiModalCacheMissError`. Nothing validates that the cached item's modality, shape, or token count matches the current request's placeholders.  **4. The mismatch is fatal to the engine.** The scheduler plans encoder work from the request's (fresh) placeholder count N_B, while the worker gathers embeddings from the stale N_A-row tensor (encoder-cache hit under the same forged hash, or re-encoding the stale data — both yield N_A rows). `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` then raises:  ```python # vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:703-714 inputs_embeds[is_multimodal] = mm_embeds_flat.to(dtype=input_dtype)   # RuntimeError ... raise ValueError(     f"Attempted to assign {expr} = {num_actual_tokens} "     f"multimodal tokens to {num_expected_tokens} placeholders") from e ```  This exception is raised inside the worker's input preparation with no per-request containment, propagates to the EngineCore busy loop's top-level handler (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py:1372`), and triggers `_send_engine_dead()`. The API server's `output_handler` receives `EngineDeadError` (`vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py:819`) and the whole process tree shuts down. (Issue #55546 independently reported this sink — "one bad multimodal item kills the entire V1 engine tree" — from an organically occurring stale cache entry; this report provides the missing deterministic, remote, single-attacker trigger.)  **Cost of the attack.** With the default `mm_processor_cache_gb=4`, one max-size Qwen2.5-VL image (12845056 pixels) caches as ~77 MB, so ~56 flood requests suffice; we used 70. Flood requests are CPU-only image decodes (~0.3 s each here) and can be issued sequentially or concurrently; the total wall-clock cost of the kill was under one minute. Models with larger `max_pixels` fill the cache in even fewer requests. Note that issuing the flood with *successful* requests does not work — they would populate P1 as well; rejection after P0 insertion is essential, and the over-long-prompt 400 is one always-available way to get it (no size limits depend on non-default flags).   ## Impact  Any unauthenticated client that can reach a multimodal vLLM endpoint (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, etc. — all accept content-part `uuid`) can **deterministically crash the entire serving instance**: the EngineCore process dies, every in-flight request fails, and the API server exits; the deployment stays down until restarted. In data-parallel or multi-API-server deployments the blast radius extends to the whole engine group (cf. the DP8 outage in #55546). The attack requires no special privileges, no non-default server flags, no race conditions, and costs under a minute of sequential requests at default cache sizes.  This is distinct from the documented "Multimodal Media UUID Security" guidance in `docs/usage/security.md`, which covers only **integrity/confidentiality** consequences of uuid collisions (a caller silently receiving another caller's media). The guidance does not mention availability, and following it does not help: the attacker here deliberately collides with *their own* uuid, and the fatal element is the missing consistency check on the P1 hit path plus the unsynchronized eviction of the two caches.  **Suggested remediation** (any one of these breaks the kill chain):  1. On a P1 receiver-cache hit, validate the cached item against the request's `mm_position` (modality and expected embedding count); on mismatch, treat it as a miss (`MultiModalCacheMissError`) or reject the request — never substitute silently. 2. Make the feature/placeholder count mismatch in `_merge_multimodal_embeddings` a per-request error instead of a fatal engine exception (also requested by #55546). 3. Bind server-side cache identity to content even when a uuid is provided (e.g. `hash(content) + uuid`), eliminating forged-hash cache hits entirely. 4. Synchronize P0/P1 evictions (the engine already pushes `invalidate` to P0 on cache-miss; eviction-direction sync would close the remaining drift).  A public fix is available here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57833

## Summary  API clients can supply arbitrary `mm_processor_kwargs` per request. vLLM forwards these values through the multimodal rendering and processing pipeline to Hugging Face and custom image/video processor constructors and calls. Resource-sensitive values such as image size, patch size, patch count, crop count, or frame count can therefore be controlled by a remote client.  For processors that upscale inputs, a single request can force an allocation large enough to terminate the API server or worker with an out-of-memory condition.  ## Affected Components  The per-request field was introduced in commit `041e29471671a3d43afedb6a749421d56ef4d3e7` and first shipped in v0.7.3. The generic forwarding path remains present in current `main`.  The Isaac path is a concrete high-amplification example:  - `ChatCompletionRequest.mm_processor_kwargs` - `OnlineRenderer` request extras - `MMProcessorInputs.hf_processor_mm_kwargs` - `BaseMultiModalProcessor.info.get_hf_processor(**hf_processor_mm_kwargs)` - `IsaacProcessingInfo.get_image_processor(**kwargs)` - `IsaacImageProcessor(**kwargs)` - `process_vision_for_patches()`  Equivalent constructor forwarding exists in InternVL-derived processors, H2OVL, Step3VL, NemotronVL, and other multimodal processors. The issue is at the shared remote-input boundary and is not limited to a fixed model list.  ## Impact  - **Availability:** one request can exhaust CPU or GPU memory and terminate a   shared service process. - **Scope:** all users of the affected service instance lose availability. - **Authentication:** vLLM's API key is optional, so deployments without an   external authentication layer are remotely reachable without privileges.  ## Remediation  Reject non-empty per-request `mm_processor_kwargs` at every API-server request schema by default. Operators serving only trusted clients can explicitly opt in to the existing override behavior. Server-level `--mm-processor-kwargs` and offline `LLM` overrides remain available.  This shared boundary covers current and future multimodal processors instead of maintaining a model-specific list or a denylist that can miss custom processor arguments.  A patch for this was merged here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58830

## Summary  An untrusted multimodal request can set `mm_processor_kwargs.code_revision`. When vLLM serves a model whose Hugging Face processor uses dynamic `auto_map` code and the operator enabled `--trust-remote-code`, this request value reaches `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained` and selects the Python revision imported by Transformers.  This lets a client replace the operator-reviewed processor module with code from another revision of the same model repository. The operator-selected model/data `revision` remains pinned; only the executed processor code changes.  Importing a Python module is arbitrary code execution in the vLLM API/renderer process. The PoC below demonstrates this with an import-time filesystem write. It is fully offline and does not require a GPU, model weights, or changes to a real Hub repository.  ## Affected snapshot  - Repository: [`vllm-project/vllm`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) - Verified commit: [`570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e) - Verified with Transformers 5.15.0 and 5.16.1 - Affected release range has not been bisected  ## Affected configuration  The vulnerable path exists when all of the following are true:  1. The served model's processor uses dynamic `auto_map.AutoProcessor` code. 2. The operator enabled `trust_remote_code`. 3. The server can fetch the request-selected revision, or it is already cached. 4. The attacker can create or otherwise control a revision in the served model repository. An example is a [Hugging Face community pull-request ref](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/repositories-pull-requests-discussions#where-in-the-git-repo-are-changes-stored) when that repository permits them. 5. A multimodal request reaches the processor path.  The default `trust_remote_code=False` configuration is not affected.  ## Attack surface  `mm_processor_kwargs` is accepted directly by public request models:  - [`TokenizeChatRequest.mm_processor_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/entrypoints/serve/tokenize/protocol.py#L111-L114) - [`ChatCompletionRequest.mm_processor_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/protocol.py#L372-L375)  `/tokenize` is particularly relevant because vLLM's authentication middleware guards only `/v1`, `/v2`, `/inference`, and `/cohere` prefixes:  - [`AuthenticationMiddleware`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/entrypoints/serve/middleware/authenticate.py#L11-L62)  Consequently, `/tokenize` remains unauthenticated even when `--api-key` is configured, unless an external proxy protects it. The vLLM [Security Guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/usage/security/#unprotected-endpoints-no-api-key-required) documents `/tokenize` as an unprotected endpoint.  ## Root cause  The request value follows this path:  1. [`OnlineRenderer.preprocess_chat`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/renderers/online_renderer.py#L406-L435) places request `mm_processor_kwargs` in prompt extras. 2. Multimodal rendering forwards those kwargs into processor construction through [`MMProcessorInputs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/renderers/base.py#L751-L760) and [`_process_multimodal_async`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/renderers/base.py#L831-L847). 3. [`MultiModalConfig.merge_mm_processor_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/config/multimodal.py#L506-L518) overlays inference values on startup values, so the request wins. 4. [`cached_get_processor_without_dynamic_kwargs`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py#L344-L375) filters only recognized processor-call keys. `code_revision` is retained as a processor-construction kwarg. 5. [`cached_processor_from_config`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py#L380-L390) pins `revision` and `trust_remote_code`, but forwards the remaining kwargs without reserving `code_revision`. 6. [`get_processor`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/570735520942b6428ae98f1eb442c6d88adae55e/vllm/transformers_utils/processor.py#L205-L245) calls `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(..., revision=revision, trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code, **kwargs)`. 7. Transformers [`AutoProcessor.from_pretrained`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.15.0/src/transformers/models/auto/processing_auto.py#L294-L302) uses `code_revision` to retrieve and import the dynamic module through [`get_class_from_dynamic_module`](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/v5.15.0/src/transformers/dynamic_module_utils.py#L474-L575), then removes it before loading processor data. This is why code comes from the attacker revision while configuration/data remain operator-pinned.  Request-time processor arguments are not separated from processor-construction arguments, and `code_revision` is not reserved.  ## Suggested remediation  1. Separate processor-construction arguments from untrusted processor-call arguments. An allowlist of supported request-time preprocessing controls is safest. 2. Reject `code_revision` and other loader/source controls in request `mm_processor_kwargs`, and pass `model_config.code_revision` explicitly as the only permitted processor-code revision. 3. Add a regression test proving a request cannot change the loaded module revision while operator pins remain effective. 4. Protect `/tokenize` with the configured authentication policy as defense in depth.  Expected safe behavior is either a 4xx response for reserved request keys or silently ignoring them before processor construction. Rejection is preferable because it makes attempted misuse visible.  A patch for this was merged here: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58830

### Summary  The Phi-4 multimodal audio encoder (`phi4mm_audio.py` / `phi4mm_utils.py`) runs its conformer attention in **eager mode by default**: the official HF config of `microsoft/Phi-4-multimodal-instruct` does not set `use_pt_scaled_dot_product_attention`, so the default `False` applies (`phi4mm_audio.py:166`, `:876`; `phi4mm_utils.py:1669`). The eager path fully materializes the attention probability matrix of shape `[n_chunks, 16, 500, 500]` per layer — and then **stores it on the module**: `self.attn = attn` (`phi4mm_utils.py:1802`, a `torch.jit.Attribute` declared at `:1693`), keeping a live reference for every one of the 24 encoder layers.  The only gates on audio length are the server-side limits `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_CLIP_FILESIZE_MB=25` and `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=600` (`envs.py:83-84`) — i.e. a 10-minute clip is a **legal input by default**. A 600 s clip becomes ~60,000 mel frames, which the encoder unfolds into 500-frame chunks (`phi4mm_audio.py:996`, `max_seq_len = 500`), giving `n_chunks ≈ 120`. Each layer therefore materializes a `120×16×500×500` matrix (~1–2 GiB depending on dtype), and the module attribute keeps all completed layers' matrices alive, so GPU memory climbs monotonically **within a single request** until an allocation fails.  Verified end-to-end on the official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0` image: one 19.2 MB silent 600 s WAV → worker `torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 2.29 GiB ... 501.75 MiB free ... 22.09 GiB allocated by PyTorch` inside `get_audio_features` (`phi4mm_audio.py:1279` → `:1332` → `phi4mm_utils.py:1386`) → `EngineCore encountered a fatal error` → API `EngineDeadError` → whole server down; `/health` refuses connections. Total time from request to dead service: **~6 seconds**.  A secondary effect: because `self.attn` persists on the module after the request ends, the matrices of the last audio request stay resident indefinitely (observed +50 MiB pinned after a single 5 s control request); they are only overwritten by the next audio request, so the resident footprint equals the largest audio processed since startup.  ### Details  **1. Root cause.** `MultiHeadedAttention.forward_attention` in eager mode computes `attn = masked_softmax(scores, mask)` and unconditionally executes `self.attn = attn` (`phi4mm_utils.py:1795-1802`). The attribute is a leftover inference/debug hook (used by `torch.jit.Attribute(None, Tensor | None)` at `:1693`); in serving it serves no purpose but pins the full `[batch·chunks, heads, T, T]` tensor per layer past both the layer's forward and the request's lifetime. The SDP attention branch (`use_pt_scaled_dot_product_attention=True`) never materializes this matrix — but the HF config does not enable it and the code default is `False`.  **2. Why one request suffices.** The conformer chunks long audio to `max_seq_len = 500` frames (`phi4mm_audio.py:996`). Duration is bounded only by `VLLM_MAX_AUDIO_DECODE_DURATION_S=600`, so `n_chunks` reaches ~120 for a maximal clip. With 16 heads and fp32 scores, one layer's attention tensor is ~1.8 GiB (the observed failing allocation was 2.29 GiB, consistent with the scores+bias materialization). The encoder has `num_blocks=24`, `attention_heads=16`, `attention_dim=1024`, `time_reduction=8` (HF config). Weights plus a handful of retained per-layer matrices exhaust the ~2.3 GiB headroom that `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9` leaves on a 24 GB card — mid-forward, on the first request.  **4. Deployment reality.** `--trust-remote-code` is the documented, standard way to serve this model (the HF model card instructs it), so the finding applies to default deployments. The crash is deterministic, not load-dependent: scheduler stats at death show a single running request and near-zero KV cache usage.   ### Impact  Any unauthenticated client that can reach the chat/completions API of a default deployment serving `Phi-4-multimodal-instruct` (or any model reusing this audio tower) can kill the entire engine with **one request** carrying a perfectly legal 10-minute audio clip (silent noise suffices — no crafted content needed). Full denial of service, requiring a process restart. On GPUs with more headroom (e.g. 80 GB at default utilization) a single request may survive, but the eager path still materializes GiB-scale per-layer matrices and retains the last request's tensors indefinitely, so a few sequential max-length requests — or normal traffic following one — achieve the same result.  Relation to prior art: the only public Phi-4-mm advisory we found, GHSA-vc6m-hm49-g9qg, concerns a CPU-side quadratic-cost path — different subsystem, different mechanism. GitHub search for "phi4mm audio OOM/memory" (31 results, 2026-10-08) shows no report of this attention-retention issue; `main` (2026-10-08) is unchanged.  **Suggested remediation** (any one breaks the chain; 1+2 recommended):  1. Remove `self.attn = attn` from the serving path (or gate it behind an explicit debug/`output_attentions` flag) so attention matrices are freed when the layer returns. 2. Default `use_pt_scaled_dot_product_attention` to `True` (flash/SDPA kernels never materialize the `[B, H, T, T]` matrix); keep eager only as an opt-in. 3. Additionally bound the encoder input (frames or duration) for this model so the eager path cannot reach GiB-scale single-layer allocations even if enabled.  This advisory was fixed in [MR60614](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60614).

## Summary  Any vLLM deployment serving a model of the DeepSeek-OCR family — `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR`, `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR-2`, or `baidu/Unlimited-OCR` (whose `UnlimitedOCRForCausalLM` subclasses `DeepseekOCRForCausalLM`) — can be **killed by a single unauthenticated chat request carrying an ordinary, schema-valid PNG image**, under completely default server configuration.  The image model's input validation contains a guard inherited from the upstream DeepSeek-OCR reference implementation:  ```python # vllm/model_executor/models/deepseek_ocr.py:478-479  (_parse_and_validate_image_input) if torch.sum(pixel_values).item() == 0:     return None ```  In the original research code this was an empty-batch shortcut; in vLLM's serving architecture `pixel_values` is the actual client image tensor, and the condition is **exactly satisfiable by a legitimate image**: the in-tree `DeepseekOCRProcessor` normalizes pixels with `ToTensor + Normalize(0.5, 0.5)` (`vllm/transformers_utils/processors/deepseek_ocr.py:120-140`), mapping pixel value 0 → exactly −1.0 and 255 → exactly +1.0 in float32. A 1024×1024 image that is half pure black and half pure white (a perfectly ordinary 1-bit-style scanned-document PNG for an OCR model) therefore yields `torch.sum(pixel_values) == 0.0` **exactly** (equal counts of ±1.0; pairwise reduction stays integer-exact, well inside float32's 2²⁴ exactness bound). `ImageOps.pad(image, (1024, 1024))` is the identity map for an already-1024×1024 image (`processors/deepseek_ocr.py:350-355`), so no padding pixels disturb the balance.  Returning `None` makes `embed_multimodal` return `None` (`deepseek_ocr.py:606-611`), which immediately trips the engine-side sanity check in the worker:  ```python # vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:512  (sanity_check_mm_encoder_outputs) assert isinstance(mm_embeddings, (list, tuple, torch.Tensor)), (     "Expected multimodal embeddings to be a list/tuple of 2D tensors, ...") ```  The `AssertionError` is raised inside the encoder runner of the EngineCore worker process with no per-request containment, escapes to the busy loop's top-level handler (`vllm/v1/engine/core.py:1368`, "EngineCore encountered a fatal error."), triggers `EngineDeadError` at the API server (`vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py:843`), and the whole process tree shuts down permanently. `/health` refuses connections until a manual restart.  Verified end-to-end on the official `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.30.0` image (id d076d77d8dad) with real `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR` weights: after confirming `/health` 200, a text chat 200, and two control images (all-white and all-black 1024×1024) 200, the single half-black/half-white request returned HTTP 500 (`EngineCore encountered an issue`), the engine log shows `AssertionError: Expected multimodal embeddings to be a list/tuple of 2D tensors ... got <class 'NoneType'>` at `v1/worker/utils.py:512`, the API server shut itself down, and the container exited (`Exited (0)`, `OOMKilled=false`). Every subsequent request, including `GET /health`, fails at the socket. The vulnerable check is unchanged on `main` (verified 2026-09-30 against the raw file on the default branch).  **Environment notes (disclosed for completeness; unrelated to the sink):** (1) the v0.30.0 image's Triton version refuses to compile `deepencoder.py`'s fused rel-pos attention kernel (`LOG2E` non-constexpr global) during the startup profile run; per the compiler's own suggestion we set `TRITON_ALLOW_NON_CONSTEXPR_GLOBALS=1` — an environment workaround only, no source file was modified. (2) DeepSeek-OCR ships no `chat_template`, so verification passed a one-line `--chat-template` that concatenates message content text; this does not touch the image data path. (3) The zero-sum check aggregates over the whole per-step modality batch, so the trigger image must be alone in its encoder batch — trivially true on an idle instance (our verification: first attempt, single request), and simply retried otherwise.  ## Details  **1. The processor maps an ordinary binary image to exactly ±1.0 pixels.** `DeepseekOCRProcessor.tokenize_with_images` (`vllm/transformers_utils/processors/deepseek_ocr.py:338-389`) builds the global view as `ImageOps.pad(image, (base_size, base_size), color=mean*255)` with `base_size = 1024` (`:21`). For a 1024×1024 input the pad is a no-op (same-size `ImageOps.contain` resampling is the identity: the bicubic kernel passes through sample points exactly). `ImageTransform` (`:120-140`) then applies `T.ToTensor()` (uint8 0 → 0.0, 255 → 1.0, exact in float32) and `T.Normalize((0.5,)*3, (0.5,)*3)` (0.0 → −1.0, 1.0 → +1.0, exact). A left-half-black/right-half-white 1024×1024 RGB image therefore produces 1,572,864 elements of −1.0 and 1,572,864 of +1.0; `torch.sum` (pairwise/tree reduction, partial sums bounded by 1.58M ≪ 2²⁴) evaluates to exactly `0.0`, and `.item() == 0` is `True`. All of this runs in the API process and passes every validation layer: the image is 1 MP, far under the default `VLLM_MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` cap of 178,956,970 (`vllm/envs.py:86`).  **2. The zero guard turns a valid image into a `None` encoder output.** `_parse_and_validate_image_input` (`deepseek_ocr.py:468-497`) returns `None` on the exact-zero sum; `embed_multimodal` (`:606-611`) propagates that `None` to its caller. The same pattern exists in `deepseek_ocr2.py:339` (`if pixel_values is None or torch.sum(pixel_values).item() == 0: return None`), and `UnlimitedOCRForCausalLM` (`unlimited_ocr.py:244`) inherits the method unmodified. (A sibling check in `_encode_local_features` at `deepseek_ocr.py:522-523` guards crop tensors, which pass through a lossy resize and are not needed for this report.)  **3. The worker asserts on the `None` and the engine dies.** With the default configuration (`cudagraph_mm_encoder=False`, `config/compilation.py`), the V2 model runner executes the encoder eagerly: `execute_model` (`v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1849`) → `model_states/default.py:108 prepare_inputs_embeds` → `encoder_runner.execute_mm_encoder` (`v1/worker/gpu/mm/encoder_runner.py:168`) → `model.embed_multimodal(**mm_kwargs_batch)` → `None` → `sanity_check_mm_encoder_outputs(batch_outputs, expected_num_items=1)` (`encoder_runner.py:170`) → `AssertionError` at `v1/worker/utils.py:512`. There is no per-request try/except anywhere on this path; the exception reaches the busy loop's top-level `except Exception` at `core.py:1368` (via `step_with_batch_queue` at `core.py:660` and `collective_rpc`), which logs "EngineCore encountered a fatal error.", sends engine-dead, and re-raises (fault tolerance off by default; `engine_core_sentinel` re-raises). The API server's `output_handler` receives `EngineDeadError` (`async_llm.py:843`) and shuts down. In the verified run the container exited (code 0, `OOMKilled=false`) and the port stayed closed — no self-recovery.  **4. Why the guard exists and why it is wrong here.** The `torch.sum(...) == 0 → return None` shortcut comes from the upstream DeepSeek-OCR reference implementation, where it skipped empty batches during batch inference. In vLLM, `embed_multimodal` is only invoked when the scheduler has real multimodal items to encode, so the guard never protects anything — it is purely a landmine that converts one specific, perfectly legal pixel distribution into a contract violation (`embed_multimodal` must return embeddings, not `None`) that the engine treats as a fatal invariant breach.  **Version history.** The check was introduced together with the model itself in #27247 ("[Model] Upstream Deepseek-OCR model", commit 675aa2ec, 2025-10-22; first stable release v0.11.1) and is unchanged since. DeepSeek-OCR-2 support (#33165, 2026-02-02) carries the same check at `deepseek_ocr2.py:339`. On `main` (checked 2026-09-30) the guard in `_parse_and_validate_image_input` is still present verbatim.  ## Impact  Any unauthenticated client that can reach the OpenAI-compatible API of a deployment serving DeepSeek-OCR, DeepSeek-OCR-2, or Unlimited-OCR can **deterministically crash the entire serving instance with one request**: the EngineCore process dies, every in-flight and future request fails, and the API server exits; absent a supervisor the deployment stays down until restarted. The trigger is a schema-valid chat request with a small, completely legal PNG — for an OCR service, a half-black/half-white bitmap is indistinguishable from ordinary scanned-document traffic. The attack costs one request (~0.1 s observed end-to-end) and can be repeated after every restart.  No special server flags, no malformed input, no resource exhaustion, and no race are involved; the only requirement is that the trigger image is alone in its per-step encoder batch (true on an idle instance and retryable otherwise). Default-configured deployments of these models are affected with no mitigation short of patching.  **Suggested remediation** (any one of these breaks the kill chain):  1. Remove the `torch.sum(pixel_values) == 0 → return None` shortcut from `_parse_and_validate_image_input` (and the `_encode_local_features` sibling) in `deepseek_ocr.py` / `deepseek_ocr2.py`: in vLLM an empty encoder batch never reaches `embed_multimodal`, so the guard protects nothing and only converts valid inputs into a contract violation. If an all-zeros fast-path is ever needed, return a correctly-shaped zero embedding, not `None`. 2. If the check is kept as input validation, enforce it where it belongs: reject the offending item with a per-request error (HTTP 400) in the API-process input pipeline, not by violating the `embed_multimodal` return contract inside the worker. 3. Defense in depth: `sanity_check_mm_encoder_outputs` failures should fail the offending request rather than the EngineCore busy loop — a model returning `None` for one item should not be engine-fatal.  This advisory was fixed in [MR59417](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59417).

### Summary  In vLLM 0.30.0, `ImageMediaIO` passes attacker-controlled image bytes to Pillow's format autodetection without restricting the accepted formats; the request's MIME label does not constrain decoder selection. An EPS payload labeled `image/png` reached the host's Ghostscript executable. On a host with Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, this exposes the known Ghostscript sandbox escape through vLLM's image-loading path and can execute commands with the vLLM process's privileges. A bounded marker-command payload executed through the PyPI wheel's actual `ImageMediaIO.load_base64()` implementation using Debian Ghostscript 10.03.0. The loader-level execution is reproduced; the HTTP request path is source-traced but was not exercised end to end. This report concerns vLLM's untrusted-format dispatch and does not claim a new Ghostscript vulnerability. Exploitation requires an image-capable request path, a caller able to reach it under the deployment's authentication policy, and a vulnerable host Ghostscript build.  ### Details  `ImageMediaIO` is the boundary where attacker-controlled bytes enter Pillow's format autodetection: the declared MIME type does not constrain decoder selection, and the loader calls `Image.open(BytesIO(data))` without a Pillow format allowlist. Pillow recognizes EPS by its file signature, and vLLM's subsequent `image.load()` call enters Pillow's EPS processing path. The OpenAI chat multimodal parser reaches this path through [`parse_image()` and `fetch_image()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/vllm/entrypoints/chat_utils.py#L1077-L1081) and the [media connector](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py#L367-L402); the data URL path extracts the MIME label and forwards the bytes to the loader ([source](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/vllm/multimodal/media/connector.py#L319-L332)). This is the vLLM-specific issue: untrusted image bytes can select a Pillow-supported format parser. Each downstream impact depends on the relevant parser, component version, and host configuration.  Pillow recognizes EPS by its file signature and invokes Ghostscript with `-dSAFER`, `-sDEVICE=pnmraw`, and the untrusted EPS input ([Pillow EPS plugin](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.3.0/src/PIL/EpsImagePlugin.py#L132-L159), [load path](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/blob/12.3.0/src/PIL/EpsImagePlugin.py#L405-L415)). The command execution in this report uses the already-known Ghostscript CVE-2024-29510, which allows crafted PostScript to bypass `-dSAFER`; Ghostscript lists 10.03.1 as the upstream fixed version ([Ghostscript CVE details](https://www.ghostscript.com/releases/cve/index.html)). This is an N-day dependency chain: CVE-2024-29510 provides the command-execution primitive, while the vLLM-specific issue is that untrusted, remotely supplied image bytes can reach the affected interpreter. No new Ghostscript flaw is claimed here.  The vLLM Python requirements declare Pillow but not Ghostscript, so this execution chain depends on a Ghostscript executable supplied by the host or deployment image. I reproduced command execution with the PyPI `vllm==0.30.0` wheel, Pillow 12.3.0, and Debian amd64 Ghostscript `10.03.0~dfsg-1`. The Codean Labs CVE-2024-29510 testkit identified that Ghostscript build as vulnerable. The adapted EPS payload ran only `touch` on a temporary marker. The marker existed after the loader call, although Pillow then raised `ValueError` because the exploit changes Ghostscript's output device. The API route was traced in source but a model-backed HTTP request was not run. Only PyPI `vllm==0.30.0` was checked; no wider affected release range or other Ghostscript vendor build is claimed.  The same input boundary also exposes a separate Pillow-only denial-of-service condition when the installed Pillow version is 12.0.0–12.2.0. CVE-2026-59203 is triggered by a negative `%%BeginBinary` byte count and causes Pillow's EPS parser to loop during `Image.open()`; it does not invoke Ghostscript or provide code execution ([Pillow advisory](https://github.com/python-pillow/Pillow/security/advisories/GHSA-pg7v-jwj7-p798)). The published [`vllm==0.30.0` requirements](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/v0.30.0/requirements/common.txt#L21) leave Pillow unpinned, so an existing environment can retain an affected Pillow version; the source at commit `bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35` requires [`pillow>=12.3.0`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/bc21cba9673cfc2256a2726b4bc32f062237cd35/requirements/common.txt#L22). In an isolated local check with Pillow 12.2.0, the official sample hung through `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes()` and `MediaConnector.fetch_image_async()`. Eight concurrent image loads occupied the connector's eight media-loading threads and left a benign image load queued. Pillow 12.3.0 rejected the sample promptly. This confirms a conditional media-processing DoS path, separate from the Ghostscript RCE chain; full HTTP-server availability was not measured.  ### Impact  When a vLLM image-processing endpoint accepts attacker-supplied content and the host has Ghostscript affected by CVE-2024-29510, a caller who can reach the endpoint can trigger command execution as the vLLM process user. API-key authentication and network access controls determine who can reach the request path. Deployments without Ghostscript or with a build fixed for CVE-2024-29510 are not affected by this execution chain. Separately, existing environments that run vLLM 0.30.0 with Pillow 12.0.0–12.2.0 are exposed to CVE-2026-59203 through the same image-format dispatch boundary; the demonstrated impact is exhaustion of media-loading workers, and this Pillow CVE does not cause RCE. The report asks vLLM to assess and address the unsafe dispatch of untrusted image bytes and the affected dependency combinations.  This advisory was fixed in [MR60022](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60022).
